example: A spinning wheel rotating at 5 rad/s has a rotational kinetic energy of 50 J. What is its moment of inertia?

name: Angular momentum of a rotating body
pattern: A turntable with a moment of inertia of <number> kg*m^<number> rotates at <number> rad/s. What is its angular momentum?
example: A turntable with a moment of inertia of 0.5 kg*m^2 rotates at 8 rad/s. What is its angular momentum?

name: Angular momentum of a rotating body
pattern: A rotating wheel has an angular momentum of <number> kg*m^<number>/s and a moment of inertia of <number> kg*m^2. What is its angular velocity?
example: A rotating wheel has an angular momentum of 12 kg*m^2/s and a moment of inertia of 3 kg*m^2. What is its angular velocity?

name: Tangential acceleration of a point on a rotating body
pattern: A point on a rotating wheel is at a radius of <number> m. The wheel has an angular acceleration of <number> rad/s^2. What is the tangential acceleration of the point?
example: A point on a rotating wheel is at a radius of 0.5 m. The wheel has an angular acceleration of 4 rad/s^2. What is the tangential acceleration of the point?

name: Tangential acceleration of a point on a rotating body
pattern: A flywheel of radius <number> m spins up with an angular acceleration of <number> rad/s^2. Find the tangential acceleration at its rim.
example: A flywheel of radius 0.3 m spins up with an angular acceleration of 10 rad/s^2. Find the tangential acceleration at its rim.

name: Centripetal acceleration from angular velocity
pattern: A centrifuge rotates at an angular velocity of <number> rad/s. What is the centripetal acceleration at a radius of <number> m?
example: A centrifuge rotates at an angular velocity of 3 rad/s. What is the centripetal acceleration at a radius of 2 m?

name: Centripetal acceleration from angular velocity
pattern: A sample spins at an angular velocity of <number> rad/s at a radius of <number> m. What is its centripetal acceleration?
example: A sample spins at an angular velocity of 100 rad/s at a radius of 0.1 m. What is its centripetal acceleration?

name: Angular momentum of a point mass on a circle
pattern: A <number> kg satellite moves at <number> m/s in a circular orbit of radius <number> m. What is its angular momentum?
example: A 2 kg satellite moves at 3 m/s in a circular orbit of radius 4 m. What is its angular momentum?

name: Angular momentum of a point mass on a circle
pattern: A planet of mass <number> kg orbits at <number> m/s at an orbital radius of <number> m. What is its angular momentum?
example: A planet of mass 5.97e24 kg orbits at 2.98e4 m/s at an orbital radius of 1.496e11 m. What is its angular momentum?

name: Absolute pressure at a depth in a fluid
pattern: The atmospheric pressure is <number> Pa. What is the absolute pressure <number> m below the surface of water of density <number> kg/m^<number>?
example: The atmospheric pressure is 101325 Pa. What is the absolute pressure 10 m below the surface of water of density 1000 kg/m^3?

name: Absolute pressure at a depth in a fluid
pattern: A diver is at a depth of <number> m in sea water of density <number> kg/m^<number> where the atmospheric pressure is <number> Pa. What is the absolute pressure on the diver?
example: A diver is at a depth of 20 m in sea water of density 1025 kg/m^3 where the atmospheric pressure is 1e5 Pa. What is the absolute pressure on the diver?

name: Flow rate as volume per time
pattern: A hose fills a <number> L bucket in <number> s with water. What is the flow rate?
example: A hose fills a 2 L bucket in 10 s with water. What is the flow rate?

name: Flow rate as volume per time
pattern: Water flows through a pipe and <number> L flows out in <number> s. What is the volume flow rate?
example: Water flows through a pipe and 300 L flows out in 60 s. What is the volume flow rate?

name: Flow rate through a cross section
pattern: Water flows through a pipe with a cross-sectional area of <number> m^<number> at a speed of <number> m/s. What is the flow rate?
example: Water flows through a pipe with a cross-sectional area of 3e-4 m^2 at a speed of 2 m/s. What is the flow rate?

name: Flow rate through a cross section
pattern: Blood is pumped at a flow rate of <number> m^<number>/s into the aorta of cross-sectional area <number> m^2. What is the speed of the blood?
example: Blood is pumped at a flow rate of 8.3e-5 m^3/s into the aorta of cross-sectional area 3.14e-4 m^2. What is the speed of the blood?

name: Thermal expansion of volume
pattern: Water with an original volume of <number> L and a coefficient of volume expansion of <number> <number>/K is heated by <number> K. What is the change in volume as it expands?
example: Water with an original volume of 1 L and a coefficient of volume expansion of 2.1e-4 1/K is heated by 50 K. What is the change in volume as it expands?

name: Thermal expansion of volume
pattern: Gasoline has a coefficient of volume expansion of <number> <number>/K. A tank holds an initial volume of <number> L and is warmed by <number> K so it expands. What is the increase in volume?
example: Gasoline has a coefficient of volume expansion of 9.5e-4 1/K. A tank holds an initial volume of 60 L and is warmed by 20 K so it expands. What is the increase in volume?

name: Efficiency of a heat engine
pattern: A heat engine takes in a heat input of <number> J and produces a work output of <number> J. What is its efficiency?
example: A heat engine takes in a heat input of 1000 J and produces a work output of 300 J. What is its efficiency?

name: Efficiency of a heat engine
pattern: An engine with an efficiency of <number> has a heat input of <number> J. What is its work output?
example: An engine with an efficiency of 0.25 has a heat input of 4000 J. What is its work output?

name: Carnot (maximum) efficiency
pattern: A heat engine works between a hot reservoir temperature of <number> K and a cold reservoir temperature of <number> K. What is its maximum efficiency?
example: A heat engine works between a hot reservoir temperature of 600 K and a cold reservoir temperature of 300 K. What is its maximum efficiency?

name: Carnot (maximum) efficiency
pattern: What is the carnot efficiency of an engine with a hot reservoir temperature of <number> K and a cold reservoir temperature of <number> K?
example: What is the carnot efficiency of an engine with a hot reservoir temperature of 873 K and a cold reservoir temperature of 293 K?

name: Maximum speed of a mass on a spring
pattern: A <number> kg mass oscillates in simple harmonic motion on a spring with a spring constant of <number> N/m and an amplitude of <number> m. What is its maximum speed?
example: A 1 kg mass oscillates in simple harmonic motion on a spring with a spring constant of 100 N/m and an amplitude of 0.1 m. What is its maximum speed?

name: Maximum speed of a mass on a spring
pattern: A <number> kg block on a spring of spring constant <number> N/m oscillates with an amplitude of <number> cm. What is its maximum velocity?
example: A 0.5 kg block on a spring of spring constant 200 N/m oscillates with an amplitude of 5 cm. What is its maximum velocity?

name: Intensity as power per area
pattern: A power of <number> W falls uniformly on an area of <number> m^2. What is the intensity?
example: A power of 100 W falls uniformly on an area of 2 m^2. What is the intensity?

name: Intensity as power per area
pattern: Sunlight with an intensity of <number> W/m^<number> falls on a panel with an area of <number> m^2. What power does it receive?
example: Sunlight with an intensity of 1000 W/m^2 falls on a panel with an area of 0.5 m^2. What power does it receive?

name: Wavelength of light in a medium
pattern: Light with a wavelength in vacuum of <number> nm enters glass with an index of refraction of 1.5. What is the wavelength in the medium?
example: Light with a wavelength in vacuum of 600 nm enters glass with an index of refraction of 1.5. What is the wavelength in the medium?

name: Wavelength of light in a medium
pattern: Yellow light of wavelength in air <number> nm enters water, refractive index 1.333. What is the wavelength in the medium?
example: Yellow light of wavelength in air 589 nm enters water, refractive index 1.333. What is the wavelength in the medium?

name: Index of refraction
pattern: The speed of light in the medium is <number> m/s for a certain glass. What is the index of refraction of the glass?
example: The speed of light in the medium is 2e8 m/s for a certain glass. What is the index of refraction of the glass?

name: Index of refraction
finds: speed of light in the material
pattern: Diamond has an index of refraction of 2.42. What is the speed of light in the material?
example: Diamond has an index of refraction of 2.42. What is the speed of light in the material?

name: Focal length of a spherical mirror
pattern: A concave mirror has a radius of curvature of <number> m. What is its focal length?
example: A concave mirror has a radius of curvature of 0.4 m. What is its focal length?

name: Focal length of a spherical mirror
pattern: A mirror has a focal length of <number> cm. What is its radius of curvature?
example: A mirror has a focal length of 15 cm. What is its radius of curvature?

name: Rms voltage of a sinusoidal supply
pattern: An AC supply has a peak voltage of <number> V. What is the rms voltage?
example: An AC supply has a peak voltage of 170 V. What is the rms voltage?

name: Rms voltage of a sinusoidal supply
pattern: Mains AC has an rms voltage of <number> V. What is its peak voltage?
example: Mains AC has an rms voltage of 230 V. What is its peak voltage?

name: Rms current of a sinusoidal supply
pattern: An AC circuit has a peak current of <number> A. What is the rms current?
example: An AC circuit has a peak current of 10 A. What is the rms current?

name: Rms current of a sinusoidal supply
pattern: An AC appliance draws an rms current of <number> A. What is the peak current?
example: An AC appliance draws an rms current of 2 A. What is the peak current?

name: Magnetic field at the centre of a circular loop
pattern: A circular loop of wire with a radius of <number> m carries a current of <number> A. What is the magnetic field at its centre?
example: A circular loop of wire with a radius of 0.1 m carries a current of 5 A. What is the magnetic field at its centre?

name: Magnetic field at the centre of a circular loop
pattern: A loop of radius <number> cm carries a current of <number> A. What magnetic field does it produce at the centre?
example: A loop of radius 5 cm carries a current of 8 A. What magnetic field does it produce at the centre?

name: Time constant of an RL circuit
pattern: An inductor of inductance <number> H is connected in series with a <number> ohm resistor. What is the time constant?
example: An inductor of inductance 0.5 H is connected in series with a 100 ohm resistor. What is the time constant?

name: Time constant of an RL circuit
pattern: You want a time constant of <number> s using an inductor and a <number> ohm resistor. What inductance is needed?
example: You want a time constant of 1 s using an inductor and a 500 ohm resistor. What inductance is needed?

name: Reactance of an inductor
pattern: An inductor of inductance <number> H is in an AC circuit at a frequency of <number> Hz. What is its reactance?
example: An inductor of inductance 0.03 H is in an AC circuit at a frequency of 60 Hz. What is its reactance?

name: Reactance of an inductor
pattern: At what frequency will an inductor of inductance <number> mH have a reactance of <number> ohm?
example: At what frequency will an inductor of inductance 30 mH have a reactance of 100 ohm?

name: Reactance of a capacitor
pattern: A capacitor with a capacitance of <number> uF is in an AC circuit at a frequency of <number> Hz. What is its reactance?
example: A capacitor with a capacitance of 1 uF is in an AC circuit at a frequency of 60 Hz. What is its reactance?

name: Reactance of a capacitor
pattern: What capacitance should a capacitor have to give a reactance of <number> ohm at <number> Hz?
example: What capacitance should a capacitor have to give a reactance of 2e6 ohm at 60 Hz?

name: Resonant frequency of an LC circuit
pattern: A resonant circuit has an inductance of <number> H and a capacitance of <number> uF. What is the resonant frequency?
example: A resonant circuit has an inductance of 0.01 H and a capacitance of 1 uF. What is the resonant frequency?

name: Resonant frequency of an LC circuit
pattern: What capacitance gives a resonant frequency of <number> GHz with an inductance of <number> nH in an LC circuit?
example: What capacitance gives a resonant frequency of 1 GHz with an inductance of 8 nH in an LC circuit?

name: Angular velocity under constant angular acceleration
pattern: A flywheel rotating at an initial angular velocity of <number> rad/s has an angular acceleration of <number> rad/s^<number> for <number> s. What is its final angular velocity?
example: A flywheel rotating at an initial angular velocity of 2 rad/s has an angular acceleration of 3 rad/s^2 for 4 s. What is its final angular velocity?

name: Angular velocity under constant angular acceleration
pattern: A turntable starts from rest and spins up with an angular acceleration of <number> rad/s^2. What is its final angular velocity after <number> s?
example: A turntable starts from rest and spins up with an angular acceleration of 0.5 rad/s^2. What is its final angular velocity after 6 s?

name: Angular velocity and angle turned under constant angular acceleration
pattern: A flywheel starts from rest and spins up with an angular acceleration of <number> rad/s^<number> through an angular displacement of <number> rad. What is its final angular velocity?
example: A flywheel starts from rest and spins up with an angular acceleration of 2 rad/s^2 through an angular displacement of 25 rad. What is its final angular velocity?

name: Angular velocity and angle turned under constant angular acceleration
pattern: A wheel rotating with an initial angular velocity of <number> rad/s has an angular acceleration of <number> rad/s^<number> over an angular displacement of <number> rad. What is its final angular velocity?
example: A wheel rotating with an initial angular velocity of 4 rad/s has an angular acceleration of 1.5 rad/s^2 over an angular displacement of 10 rad. What is its final angular velocity?

name: Energy balance of a cyclic heat engine
pattern: A heat engine takes in a heat input of <number> J and has <number> J of heat rejected per cycle. What is its work output?
example: A heat engine takes in a heat input of 1000 J and has 700 J of heat rejected per cycle. What is its work output?

name: Energy balance of a cyclic heat engine
pattern: A power plant engine has a heat input of <number> J and a work output of <number> J. How much heat is rejected?
example: A power plant engine has a heat input of 6e5 J and a work output of 2.5e5 J. How much heat is rejected?

name: Coefficient of performance of a refrigerator
pattern: A refrigerator has <number> J of heat removed using a work input of <number> J. What is its coefficient of performance?
example: A refrigerator has 1200 J of heat removed using a work input of 400 J. What is its coefficient of performance?

name: Coefficient of performance of a refrigerator
pattern: A freezer with a coefficient of performance of <number> uses a work input of <number> J. How much heat is removed?
example: A freezer with a coefficient of performance of 4 uses a work input of 250 J. How much heat is removed?

name: Coefficient of performance of a heat pump
pattern: A heat pump delivers <number> J of heat delivered for a work input of <number> J. What is its coefficient of performance?
example: A heat pump delivers 1500 J of heat delivered for a work input of 500 J. What is its coefficient of performance?

name: Coefficient of performance of a heat pump
pattern: A heat pump with a coefficient of performance of <number> uses a work input of <number> J. How much heat is delivered?
example: A heat pump with a coefficient of performance of 3.5 uses a work input of 2000 J. How much heat is delivered?

name: Radius of a charged particle's circle in a magnetic field
pattern: A proton of mass <number> kg and charge <number> C moves at <number> m/s perpendicular to a magnetic field of <number> T. What is the radius of the circular path?
example: A proton of mass 1.67e-27 kg and charge 1.6e-19 C moves at 1e6 m/s perpendicular to a magnetic field of 0.5 T. What is the radius of the circular path?

name: Radius of a charged particle's circle in a magnetic field
pattern: An electron of mass <number> kg and charge <number> C moves at <number> m/s perpendicular to a magnetic field of <number> T. What is the radius of its path?
example: An electron of mass 9.11e-31 kg and charge 1.6e-19 C moves at 7.5e6 m/s perpendicular to a magnetic field of 1e-5 T. What is the radius of its path?

name: Time constant of an RC circuit
pattern: An RC circuit has a resistor of <number> ohm and a capacitor of <number> uF. What is the time constant?
example: An RC circuit has a resistor of 1000 ohm and a capacitor of 8 uF. What is the time constant?

name: Time constant of an RC circuit
pattern: A capacitor of <number> uF discharges through a resistor in an RC circuit with a time constant of <number> ms. What is the resistance?
example: A capacitor of 4 uF discharges through a resistor in an RC circuit with a time constant of 2 ms. What is the resistance?

name: Voltage of a discharging capacitor
pattern: A capacitor of <number> uF with an initial voltage of <number> V discharges through a <number> ohm resistor. What is the voltage across the capacitor after <number> ms?
example: A capacitor of 8 uF with an initial voltage of 12 V discharges through a 1000 ohm resistor. What is the voltage across the capacitor after 8 ms?

name: Voltage of a discharging capacitor
pattern: A <number> uF capacitor discharges through a <number> ohm resistor from an initial voltage of <number> V. What is the voltage across the capacitor after <number> ms?
example: A 2 uF capacitor discharges through a 500 ohm resistor from an initial voltage of 10 V. What is the voltage across the capacitor after 2 ms?

name: Voltage of a charging capacitor
pattern: An uncharged <number> uF capacitor starts charging through a <number> ohm resistor from a <number> V emf. What is the voltage across the capacitor after <number> ms?
example: An uncharged 8 uF capacitor starts charging through a 1000 ohm resistor from a 9 V emf. What is the voltage across the capacitor after 8 ms?

name: Voltage of a charging capacitor
pattern: A <number> uF capacitor is charged through a <number> ohm resistor by a <number> V emf. What is the voltage across the capacitor after <number> ms?
example: A 1 uF capacitor is charged through a 1500 ohm resistor by a 20 V emf. What is the voltage across the capacitor after 3 ms?

name: Thermal expansion of an area
pattern: A steel plate with an original area of <number> m^<number> and a coefficient of linear expansion of <number> <number>/K is heated by <number> K. What is the change in area?
example: A steel plate with an original area of 2.0 m^2 and a coefficient of linear expansion of 12e-6 1/K is heated by 50 K. What is the change in area?

name: Thermal expansion of an area
pattern: An aluminium sheet has an original area of <number> m^<number> and a coefficient of linear expansion of <number> <number>/K. By how much does its area increase when it warms by <number> K? What is the change in area?
example: An aluminium sheet has an original area of 0.5 m^2 and a coefficient of linear expansion of 24e-6 1/K. By how much does its area increase when it warms by 100 K? What is the change in area?

name: Emf of a rod moving through a magnetic field
pattern: A rod of length <number> m slides along rails at <number> m/s through a magnetic field of <number> T. What is the motional emf?
example: A rod of length 0.2 m slides along rails at 3 m/s through a magnetic field of 0.5 T. What is the motional emf?

name: Emf of a rod moving through a magnetic field
pattern: A rod of length <number> m slides along rails through a magnetic field of <number> T and an emf of <number> V is induced. What is its speed?
example: A rod of length 0.5 m slides along rails through a magnetic field of 0.4 T and an emf of 1.2 V is induced. What is its speed?

name: Current dying away in an RL circuit
pattern: In an RL circuit with an inductor and a time constant of <number> ms, an initial current of <number> A is switched off. What is the current after <number> ms?
example: In an RL circuit with an inductor and a time constant of 2.5 ms, an initial current of 10 A is switched off. What is the current after 2.5 ms?

name: Current dying away in an RL circuit
pattern: An inductor carries an initial current of <number> A when the circuit is switched off; the time constant is <number> ms. What is the current after <number> ms?
example: An inductor carries an initial current of 4 A when the circuit is switched off; the time constant is 2 ms. What is the current after 4 ms?
